result.rationale: In deleteEvent, the diff changes the fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since that branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the find predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never match, so calendarId is undefined and calendar.events.delete is invoked with an undefined calendarId — a regression from the old fallback. Same broken pattern appears in updateEvent. The mechanism is fully verifiable from the diff lines.

The old fallback to event.destinationCalendar.externalId is dead; calendarId becomes undefined and calendar.events.delete is called with calendarId: undefined, so cancellations of bookings lacking a stored externalCalendarId fail instead of deleting the event.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the calendar ID like `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` (see the changed lines around `selectedCalendar` in `updateEvent` and `calendarId` in `deleteEvent`). When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`, so it will not match the intended destination calendar (unless a calendar has `externalId` actually `undefined`). This makes the fallback to the event’s destination calendar effectively dead and can yield `undefined` for the calendarId/selectedCalendar, breaking the intended deletion/update behavior for bookings without a stored `externalCalendarId` (at minimum it won’t select the correct destination calendar).
